R118.note: JWT::decode with an HS256 Key verifies the signature correctly, but the code falls back to the hardcoded secret 'your-secret-key' when $_ENV['JWT_SECRET'] is unset (and $_ENV is empty under PHP's default variables_order), so a forged admin token signed with that public placeholder is accepted - a new CWE-798 weakness the write-up does not disclose.

R119.note: Secure=true closes the finding; the added SameSite=Strict (default is browser Lax) is stated but drops the remember-me cookie on every top-level cross-site navigation into the site, so a user arriving via an external link is treated as logged out - a restriction beyond the fix.

R120.note: execFile('whois', [domain]) removes the shell, closing the command-injection vector with the right API; a leading '-' domain could still be read as a whois option (no '--' guard), which is a separate CWE-88 residual, not the reported vector.

R121.note: require_http_methods(['POST']) is the right fix and lets CsrfViewMiddleware enforce the token, but the settings page's existing <a href> link now gets 405 until the template is changed to a csrf_token form; the write-up implies this ('forces clients to submit an HTML form') without naming the template update as a required follow-up.

R122.note: Calling the model field's validators before objects.create() does run the magic-byte check and blocks bad uploads, but it is the wrong shape: a django.core ValidationError raised inside create() is not translated by DRF's exception handler, so rejected uploads surface as a 500 rather than a 400 - putting validate_file_content on the serializer FileField (validators=[...]) or in validate_file() is the idiomatic place.

R123.note: SHA-256 hash allowlist before loading (plus collectible ALC) closes the vector with a sound mechanism, but the allowlist ships empty so every upload - including legitimate admin plugins - returns 401 until hashes are added; the write-up states admins must populate it, and it also adds a .dll extension check the original did not have.

R124.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) forces ownership to the requester on create, matching the IsExpenseReportOwner boundary; owner remains a writable field on update, but that is pre-existing and outside the reported sink.

R125.note: simple_eval closes the eval() code-injection vector and rejects unknown names, but its defaults still evaluate comparisons, conditionals, string ops, attribute access and calls to its built-in functions (rand, int, float, str), so the contract's 'any syntax outside arithmetic on those names is rejected' is not met - an operators/functions restriction or an ast-walker limited to BinOp/UnaryOp/Name/Constant would; no version pinned.

R126.note: aes.NewCipher with a random IV prepended is the right replacement and the format change is stated, but unpadded CBC CryptBlocks now panics for any upload whose length is not a multiple of 16 (previously 8), so uploads of e.g. 24 bytes that succeeded before now fail, and that is not mentioned.

R127.note: finfo magic-byte allowlist plus a server-generated name with a type-derived extension closes the double-extension vector cleanly, but the fix also adds a 5 MB size limit the original did not have (present only in code, not in the explanation) and discards the original filename the case says is wanted for a recognizable uploads listing.

R128.note: Adding %255s bounds the write into nameBuf, not the read from line: on a 64-byte non-NUL-terminated buffer with no whitespace, %255s still scans up to 255 characters past the 7 consumed by %7s, and glibc's sscanf strlen()s the input up front regardless, so the out-of-bounds read of line remains - the fix needs a NUL-terminated copy (LINE_CAPACITY+1) before sscanf.

R129.note: Rejecting '', '.', '..' and any forward or back slash before joining onto the realpath()-canonicalized base makes the name a single component, which matches the file's stated 'no subdirectories' contract; the dead 403 branch becomes a live 400, which is the fix.

R130.note: Switching to {{ }} escapes the description and closes the XSS with the correct Blade mechanism, but the value is named descriptionHtml and the contract says allowed formatting must survive if rich text is supported; escaping renders any legitimate markup as literal tags, and the write-up asserts display is preserved rather than acknowledging that loss or sanitizing in the presenter.

R131.note: Same-host check on absolute URIs blocks http(s)://evil.com, but a scheme-relative '//evil.com/x' has isAbsolute()==false and passes straight to sendRedirect, which Tomcat resolves to http://evil.com - the open redirect is only partially closed; legitimate relative and same-host redirects still work.

R132.note: lockoutOnFailure: true enables Identity's built-in lockout (LockoutEnabled defaults true for new users), which is the intended defence; locked-out users receive the generic failure message, which is acceptable.

R133.note: proc_open with an argument array and '--' is the right shape, but ['inherit'] is not a valid descriptor spec - verified with PHP 8.5 in the scratch directory: proc_open emits 'inherit is not a valid descriptor spec/mode' and returns false - so the fallback never runs and convert_document silently returns '' for every legitimate fallback conversion; omitting the descriptor entries (or using ['null'] to keep output discarded per the contract) would work.
